lead.headline: Treasury launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' against Iran
lead.dek: Nearly 60 entities and vessels sanctioned; Trump to press foreign leaders to cut Tehran off
body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday unveiled the campaign the administration had billed as an economic D-Day, naming it Operation Economic Outcast and sanctioning nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels tied to Iranian oil smuggling, nuclear and missile procurement and cyber operations.

Secondary sanctions expand into digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping, and Treasury suspended licenses that had allowed certain payments to Iran. Bessent said a major financial institution doing business with Tehran will be sanctioned by week's end. "Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime," he said.

Trump is to call foreign leaders personally to press them to drop specific Iranian trade; China buys about 90% of Iran's oil exports. Iran's security chief vowed a "seismic" response, while Pakistan said talks in Tehran on ending the war made significant progress.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court pauses ruling against Trump mail-voting order
briefs.summary: The unsigned order covers 23 states and D.C. while appeals proceed; the three liberal justices dissented, and an injunction on Postal Service enforcement stands.

briefs.headline: Crews reach 27% containment on Reno's Hawk Fire
briefs.summary: At least 32 homes are destroyed; mandatory evacuations eased from 42,000 people to 23,000 near the 15,000-acre, human-caused fire.

briefs.headline: State Department to revoke 200,000 visas of asylum seekers
briefs.summary: Visitor visas issued since 2016 to people who later filed asylum claims would be canceled on a rolling basis; revocation alone does not deport anyone.

briefs.headline: Navy families evacuated from Bahrain remain in limbo
briefs.summary: More than 1,300 dependents flown out March 2 are still in hotels and rentals with no return date; the Navy wants them to pick permanent stations.

briefs.headline: Tornado injures at least 31 in southern French village
briefs.summary: The twister tore roofs from homes in Pomas, in the Aude, during an orange storm alert, uprooting trees and cutting power across the southwest.

briefs.headline: Colombia's new president orders raids on undocumented migrants
briefs.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella's order targets about 527,000 people, most of them Venezuelan, reversing July's grant of 2.3 million temporary residence permits.

briefs.headline: Pakistan reports 'significant progress' in Iran-US talks
briefs.summary: Army chief Asim Munir met President Pezeshkian in Tehran on reviving the lapsed June ceasefire framework and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

briefs.headline: Indonesia turns to cloud seeding as peatland fires spread
briefs.summary: Nearly 940 square kilometers burned in July; haze has crossed into Malaysia and Brunei, 72 people are arrested for arson, and 30 aircraft are water-bombing.

briefs.headline: Jury awards ex-Marshall player $9.25M over Times murder story
briefs.summary: An Alabama jury found The New York Times defamed Kai Spears, represented by a Beckley attorney, by falsely placing him at a 2023 murder scene - the paper's first such loss in over 50 years.

briefs.headline: State's big power users back a delay in the MARL line case
briefs.summary: The state's biggest industrial power users agreed the PSC should pause NextEra's 107.5-mile application after late route changes; opposition letters run 6,757 to 152.

regional.item: City council advanced the Flock camera ordinance to a second reading, voting down misdemeanor penalties 6-4.
Police identified the four men killed in Friday's interstate crash as Raleigh County residents, 20 and 21.
The county assessor cut two positions Friday, about $130,000 in savings against a budget shortfall.

fishing.line: 134 cfs and falling - prime wading water.
Sound highs 6:39 a.m. and 7:16 p.m.; water 83.3F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.

briefs.headline: Ocean surface heat sets a record as El Niño strengthens
briefs.summary: Copernicus measured the global sea surface at 21.1C over the weekend, past March 2024's record and out of season for August; El Niño may peak by January.

briefs.headline: NASA finds Earth microbes could endure at the lunar south pole
briefs.summary: Goddard modeling in Science Advances says organisms carried by astronauts could persist in shadowed polar niches, muddying searches for native lunar chemistry.

briefs.headline: People past 110 carry an outsized force of killer T cells
briefs.summary: University of Osaka researchers report in Cell Reports that CD4 cytotoxic cells rise from 4% of the pool in the 70-99 group to 17.6% in supercentenarians.

briefs.headline: Depression disrupts the birth of new neurons, cell atlas shows
briefs.summary: Columbia researchers profiling about 500,000 hippocampal cells found impaired neurogenesis and stressed circuits in depressed brains, in Nature Medicine.

art.caption: The Treasury podium, department seal front and center, flags hung at its back for Monday's sanctions announcement.

kicker: Nicholas, Webster and Summers were quiet; Vermont and Prince George sat out the away desk.
